clue.text: Rap over the knuckles? This could make gent ill

definitions.meaning: the surface reading: a reprimand, figuratively a smack on the hand
the setter's reading: the answer, taken as a recipe, is a word plus an instruction that jumbles it into these seven letters

explanation.surface: A scolding so harsh it leaves a gentleman feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the recipe. Take TELLING, apply OFF as an anagram signal, and you get GENT ILL. The question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative smack on the hand is the everyday British phrase for a scolding.

clue.text: Can opener in your mini

parts.note: a tin is a can, as for food

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A tiny can opener packed in your small car or bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can opener' reads as one kitchen gadget, but Can is TIN and 'opener in' takes the first letter of your.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini, as an adjective, means very small, which is what tiny means.

clue.text: Places old cat gets surrounded by big ones

indicators.note: the preceding letters are placed inside what follows

parts.note: lions are big cats, 'ones' standing for cats
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An elderly house cat finds itself among lions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big ones' only makes sense by borrowing the word before it: 'ones' stands in for cats, so the clue gets double duty from a single noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both name spots or sites where something is found.

clue.text: Children in the US signed up

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow
in a down clue, reading upwards turns the letters round

explanation.surface: Kids in America have been enrolled in something.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is used formally and legally for a person's descendants, as in 'died without issue'.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal and formal sense: a person's direct descendants, as in wills and titles.

clue.text: Judged client in audition

indicators.note: audition is hearing, so the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a guest is a hotel's client; said out loud it matches a past tense meaning estimated

explanation.surface: A casting director assessed a customer who turned up to audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' pretends to be a stage tryout; here it means the act of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: In the sense of estimating: forming an opinion without full knowledge.

clue.text: Discovered half of shed is built

explanation.surface: Someone found out a garden shed is only half built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' does not say which half; only ED fits.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a building is to lay its base, so to establish or put it up.

clue.text: Prevent beer bellies returning

indicators.note: going back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a pot, or pot belly, is a paunch

explanation.surface: A resolution to stop beer guts coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: A beer belly is also called a pot belly, or just a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to halt something before it can happen.

clue.text: Test result finally upset Den

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: only its last letter is used

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down; in a down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: A test result finally upset someone called Den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T from result; 'upset' turns LAIR over to RIAL, the currency of Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a test of performance or quality, as in a trial run.

clue.text: Nine thumps? Barbaric chastisement

indicators.note: savage, so the letters are roughly mangled

explanation.surface: Nine blows as a penalty: a brutal beating.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a punishment, which is why the anagram hides so well.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastisement is the formal word for a penalty inflicted for wrongdoing.

clue.text: I caught husband coated in adhesive mixture

indicators.note: the letters are covered on both sides by the next word

parts.note: c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they caught their husband covered in glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' and 'husband' read as a domestic confession; both are single-letter abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A work blending borrowed styles is a medley, so a mixture.

clue.text: Prison's thieves

definitions.note: 'Prison's' is read as 'prison is'; 'thieves' is the verb, as in 'he thieves'
definitions.meaning: British slang for a jail or police station, with 's = is
read as a verb: British slang for steals

explanation.surface: A prison full of thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang: the nick is prison (also a police station) and to nick is to steal. 'Thieves' must be read as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang: a jail or police cell, and the verb to steal.

clue.text: Cautioned about training

indicators.note: turned around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was warned about their training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads like 'concerning'; here it tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: schooling, the training of the mind.

clue.text: Beginning to shed a bit of hair? Edward's worried

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept from the word that follows

parts.note: a tress is a lock or curl of hair
Ed is the usual short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward is anxious because he has started losing his hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to shed' reads as the start of balding; it only takes the first letter. The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under strain or pressure is anxious, tense and uneasy, a common everyday synonym.

clue.text: Cheers the Parisian's stories

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks, like 'cheers'

explanation.surface: A toast to a Frenchman's anecdotes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain both 'cheers' and 'ta' mean thank you. A Parisian word for 'the' is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: narratives, often invented ones.

clue.text: Be aware of rise in value

definitions.meaning: to recognise or understand a point
what an asset does as its price climbs

explanation.surface: Advice to notice when an investment is going up.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses share a root but are used in quite different worlds: understanding and finance.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to recognise the worth of something, and for an asset to gain in price.

clue.text: Go for scheme I'd oddly dismissed

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are thrown out, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone backs a plan even though their own part in it was oddly thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go for' looks like a single phrase meaning choose; the definition is just 'Go', and 'for' is PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to move forward or carry on.

clue.text: Being cross with one pop star after end of performance

indicators.note: the last letter of the next word
the pieces before it come after this letter

explanation.surface: A pop star is annoyed once the show is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' wants to mean angry, but it is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: As a participle, being means having existence now, as in 'for the time being'.

clue.text: Editor rejected request for lecture

indicators.note: thrown back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a claim is a demand or request

explanation.surface: An editor turned down a request to give a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' reads as refused; it only turns ED round.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak in a loud, formal, rhetorical way, as a lecturer might.

clue.text: Confident vet raises cuckoo

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A self-assured vet rears a cuckoo chick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' poses as the bird being raised; it means mad and mixes up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: self-assured and forceful in stating views.

clue.text: Regretting keeping small hotel running

indicators.note: holding the next letters inside

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone regrets running a tiny hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' tempts as 'managing' the hotel; it is the definition, meaning hurrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: hurrying, moving at speed.

clue.text: Wave perhaps gets moving on river

indicators.note: the letters are shifted around

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A surfer's wave gets moving along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks a wave as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: waving a hand is one of many meaningful bodily movements.

clue.text: Essentially political motive for crime

indicators.note: at its essence, the heart of the word

explanation.surface: The motive behind the crime was basically political.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' reads as 'basically'; it takes the central letter of a nine-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: betraying one's country is one specific offence.

clue.text: Teacher initially goes on about student trips

indicators.note: the first letter of the word before it
placed around the next letter

parts.note: to rave is to go on enthusiastically
L = learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A teacher starts talking at length about a school trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes on' is two words for one piece, and 'about' wraps it round the student.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: journeys, as in a person's time abroad.

clue.text: The chap's enthralled by court case

indicators.note: held captive inside the next piece

parts.note: ct = court, as in street addresses

explanation.surface: A man is gripped by a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court case' reads as a lawsuit; split it so 'case' is a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A large strong box for storing things, the container sense of case.

clue.text: The King's constrained by tunnel vision

indicators.note: held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A monarch is hampered by a narrow outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King' suggests a crowned monarch (R or K); it is a singer's nickname. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Presley's nickname was the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: Typical celebrity — eating and drinking, primarily

indicators.note: swallowing the next word inside
first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The usual celebrity lifestyle, mostly food and drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating and drinking' looks like a single pair; only 'eating' is an instruction, and 'and' is swallowed whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: normal, usual, what is expected.

clue.text: Follow mother's teaching

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: Advice to obey your mother's instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's teaching' looks like one phrase; the 's is 'is', splitting wordplay from definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed body of doctrine, the teaching of a church or party.

clue.text: Festivity's no good, regrettably

indicators.note: take the following letter away

parts.note: a gala is a festivity; 's = is, giving GALA'S

explanation.surface: The party is no fun, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' reads as a verdict on the party; it just strikes out G.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection of sorrow, used where one would say regrettably.

clue.text: Dancing at nude rave, wanting a thrilling experience

indicators.note: the letters are moving about
lacking, so a letter is removed

explanation.surface: Dancing naked at a party, in search of a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' pretends to mean desiring; it means lacking, and the 'a' after it is the letter lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an exciting or daring undertaking.

clue.text: Gran? Not an awful cook

explanation.surface: Protesting that grandma is not a terrible cook.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface defends Gran's cooking; 'cook' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: cooking under direct heat is one method of cooking.

clue.text: Comfort guy scratching head

indicators.note: striking out the first letter

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.surface: Soothing a man who is scratching his head in puzzlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man; it is the old verb meaning to ridicule, which loses its head T.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, as a noun or verb: relief from pain or worry.

clue.text: Wraps pens we damaged, but not with rags

indicators.note: broken up, so the letters are rearranged
leave the named letter out

explanation.surface: Someone wraps broken pens but refuses to use old cloths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rags' seems to be cleaning cloths; it is slang for low-grade papers. With the W gone, 10 letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is disparaging slang for a low-quality paper.
